bibliographic.title: Systemic risk governance in a dynamical model of a banking system
bibliographic.citation_apa: Fatone, L., & Mariani, F. (2018). Systemic risk governance in a dynamical model of a banking system. arXiv preprint arXiv:1812.06973.

methodology.method_family: mathematical modeling, stochastic differential equations, optimal control, statistical simulation
methodology.study_design: dynamical model with numerical simulation experiments
methodology.sample_description: homogeneous population of banks represented as log-monetary reserves in a stochastic differential equation system
methodology.technology_context: stochastic differential equation banking system model with inter-bank and bank-monetary authority cooperation parameters alpha and gamma

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The paper governs systemic risk in a mathematical banking model via optimal control; it does not address LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, or conversational governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Automated screening matched governance, banking, regulated, risk, and interaction terms, but the text shows these refer to systemic risk control in a stochastic banking model, inter-bank borrowing/lending dynamics, and monetary authority regulation. There is no mention of large language models, chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, human-AI oversight, or conversational interfaces. The work is a 2018 quantitative finance preprint outside the review's technology and governance scope.

appraisal.notes: Methodologically appropriate for mathematical systemic risk modeling, but not empirically grounded in real banking data within the provided excerpts. No discussion of AI, conversational systems, or LLM governance.

cerqual.explanation: High confidence that the study is not relevant to conversational governance of LLM-based systems; within its own domain the abstract presents a coherent optimal-control governance method, but provided text does not support synthesis for the review question.

coding.subtheme: Optimal control of cooperation parameters via mean field approximation

synthesis.main_claim: Systemic risk probability in a banking system can be governed between two thresholds by choosing an ideal bank reserve trajectory and solving an optimal control problem that sets inter-bank and monetary-authority cooperation rules over time.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a mathematical governance mechanism tested quarterly over a two-year simulation period, including scenarios with positive and negative shocks.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from evidence synthesis; may serve only as an out-of-scope example of non-AI systemic risk governance in regulated banking if a background contrast is needed.

evidence.claim: Paper title and publication context identify a 2018 arXiv quantitative finance preprint on banking systemic risk.
evidence.excerpt: arXiv:1812.06973v1 [q-fin.RM] 17 Dec 2018 Systemic risk governance in a dynamical model of a banking system

evidence.claim: Governance target is systemic risk probability in a banking SDE model, not AI or conversational system governance.
evidence.excerpt: A method to govern the probability of systemic risk in a bounded time interval is presented. The goal of the governance is to keep the probability of systemic risk in a bounded time interval between two given thresholds.

evidence.claim: Technology context is a stochastic differential equation model of bank reserves with cooperation parameters.
evidence.excerpt: The banking system model consists in an initial value problem for a system of stochastic differential equations whose dependent variables are the log-monetary reserves of the banks as functions of time.

evidence.claim: Regulated banking context involves monetary authority and bank cooperation mechanisms.
evidence.excerpt: Two distinct mechanisms are used to model the cooperation among banks and the cooperation between banks and monetary authority. These mechanisms are regulated respectively by the parameters α and γ.

evidence.claim: Interaction refers to inter-bank borrowing and lending dynamics, not conversational interaction.
evidence.excerpt: The interaction mechanism among banks given by (5) is based on the idea that "who has more gives to those who have less", and is a simple form of cooperative behaviour between banks.

evidence.claim: Governance decisions are implemented through optimal control of model parameters over time.
evidence.excerpt: The solution of the optimal control problem determines the parameters α and γ as functions of time, that is defines the rules of the borrowing and lending activity among banks and between banks and monetary authority.

evidence.claim: Evaluation uses statistical simulation with quarterly governance decisions over a two-year period.
evidence.excerpt: during a two year period we consider the governance of systemic risk in the next year when governance decisions are taken quarterly.

evidence.claim: No LLM, generative AI, or conversational AI content appears in the provided text.
evidence.excerpt: Given an interacting system made of agents that can fail individually, the systemic risk associated to the system is the risk that a large number of agents fails simultaneously leading to the failure of the entire system.
